decision_log.decision: claim_type = source_defined (Pulitzer-Drama-winners ∩ Tony-Best-Play-winners closed canonical intersection)
decision_log.rationale: Per cycle-1 audit. Both Wikipedia masters are authoritative tabulations of their respective prize-winner canonical lists; intersection is mechanically computable + closed canonical; 19 entries per current master state.

decision_log.decision: Drop Year Premiered column per cycle-1 audit required edit #1 (schema 5→4 cols)
decision_log.rationale: Both Wikipedia award-page masters tabulate Play + Playwright + award year — they do NOT uniformly tabulate premiere year. Staging Year Premiered would have required per-play Wikipedia page extraction (19+ per-play articles) inflating source_count from 2 to 21+ + introducing Broadway-premiere-vs-world-premiere ambiguity for some plays (e.g., I Am My Own Wife premiered Off-Broadway). Cleaner 4-col schema matches master support.

decision_log.decision: Operational predicate = explicit Pulitzer winner row ∩ Tony Best Play winner row (NOT Pulitzer dagger marker) per cycle-1 audit required edit #2
decision_log.rationale: Pulitzer-master notes describe '†' as marking Tony Best Play winners — but the Pulitzer table includes both winner rows AND finalist rows for each year, and the dagger appears on Tony-winning rows REGARDLESS of Pulitzer winner/finalist status. Example: 2003 Pulitzer table has winner row 'Anna in the Tropics' (Cruz) plus finalist rows 'The Goat or Who Is Sylvia?' (Albee) and 'Take Me Out' (Greenberg) — both finalist rows also carry the '†' dagger because they won Tony Best Play 2002 and 2003 respectively. Dagger-only filtering would incorrectly include both 2003 Pulitzer finalists in the dual-winner universe. The correct operational predicate uses explicit winner-row intersection: Pulitzer is_winner=TRUE rows ∩ Tony is_winner=TRUE rows.

decision_log.decision: Play labels staged from Pulitzer master (preserves subtitle specificity) per cycle-1 audit required edit #3
decision_log.rationale: Pulitzer master labels carry full play titles with subtitles ('Doubt: A Parable' / 'Angels in America: Millennium Approaches' / 'August: Osage County') while Tony master sometimes labels with shorter common forms ('Doubt'). Staging from Pulitzer labels (a) preserves subtitle specificity for benchmark calibration; (b) disambiguates 'Angels in America: Millennium Approaches' (Part One — 1993 Pulitzer + 1993 Tony) from 'Angels in America: Perestroika' (Part Two — separate 1994 Tony Best Play winner; NOT in 19-row universe because Part Two did not win Pulitzer); (c) matches more authoritative source for play-identity since Pulitzer Drama citation is the canonical scholarly reference.

decision_log.decision: Who's Afraid of Virginia Woolf? (Albee 1963) EXCLUDED from universe per audit confirmation
decision_log.rationale: Albee's play won Tony Best Play 1963 but the Pulitzer board declined to award any Drama Pulitzer that year overruling the jury's recommendation. Pulitzer winner-row membership is false (no Pulitzer was officially awarded for 1963 Drama); intersection-membership is false. Tests benchmark's strict-source-rendering policy (jury-recommended-but-board-declined cases excluded preserving source_defined cleanly).

decision_log.decision: Musical Pulitzer Drama winners (Sunday in the Park with George 1985 / Rent 1996 / Next to Normal 2010 / Hamilton 2016 / A Strange Loop 2020) AUTO-EXCLUDED from universe
decision_log.rationale: These musicals won Pulitzer Drama but Tony Best MUSICAL (not Tony Best Play — Tony Awards have separate Best Play and Best Musical categories). Tony Best Play winner-row membership is false for any musical. Intersection auto-excludes without explicit musical-filter — a clean property of the {Pulitzer Drama} ∩ {Tony Best Play} predicate. No curator judgment needed.

decision_log.decision: Pulitzer/Tony year-offset = Clybourne Park (2011/2012) only edge
decision_log.rationale: 18 of 19 staged rows have Pulitzer Year = Tony Year (same calendar year for both awards). Clybourne Park is the one 1-year-offset case: Pulitzer Drama 2011 announcement (April 2011) + Tony Best Play 2012 ceremony (June 2012) reflects the play's Off-Broadway 2010 → Broadway 2012 production trajectory (Tony eligibility opened with Broadway transfer). Both years staged as separate cells; benchmark tests for this normalization.

decision_log.decision: Co-authored play (The Diary of Anne Frank) Playwright = 'Albert Hackett; Frances Goodrich' (semicolon-delim, Hackett-first per Pulitzer master)
decision_log.rationale: Only co-authored play in 19-row universe. Semicolon-delim matches benchmark cross-instance convention (films multi-director cells / monarchs multi-house cells / heritage transboundary multi-country cells). Hackett-first ordering matches Pulitzer master's verbatim credit order.

decision_log.decision: Category = set_operation primary + set_filter secondary; operation_type = intersect
decision_log.rationale: Per cycle-1 audit confirmation + cycle-2 audit normalized-identity-join clarification. db_analog models the prize-winner-set intersection via INNER JOIN on `normalize_play_identity(play_title)` (semantically equivalent to INTERSECT on canonical-play-identity dimension — accommodates 'Doubt: A Parable' vs 'Doubt' cross-master label-form difference). Genuine set-arithmetic at source level: two authoritative prize-winner sets intersected on normalized play identity. Mirror precedent `aau_big_ten_intersection_universities` + `unesco_world_heritage_mixed_sites_attributes` + `physicists_who_were_nobel_laureates`.

No prior pkdb_bench Theater instance. Culture family extends from 10 to 11 instances (joining Film + Music + Literature + Architecture + Philosophy + Visual-Arts + Gaming + Heritage; Theater is genuinely novel).

Per cycle-1 audit lock. Plays are artifacts (creative works) not events (the awards are events but the benchmark entity is the play itself). Mirror precedent: artifacts/films + artifacts/books + artifacts/songs + artifacts/video-games — plays fit this bucket cleanly. NEW fine-class extends artifacts bucket from 4 to 5 fine-classes.

decision_log.decision: Sort = Pulitzer Year ASC + Play ASC tiebreak
decision_log.rationale: Pulitzer Year ASC orders the universe chronologically by first-prize-year (since Pulitzer and Tony years usually match; Clybourne Park's Tony 2012 sorted under Pulitzer 2011 maintains chronological consistency). Play ASC tiebreak is defensive — no Pulitzer-Year ties in the 19-row staged universe.

decision_log.decision: Cycle-2 HYGIENE fix: db_analog INNER JOIN on normalized_play_id (NOT raw play_title)
decision_log.rationale: Per cycle-1 post-staging audit's NON-BLOCKING HYGIENE. Original db_analog used `INNER JOIN ON p.play_title = t.play_title` which would miss-match 'Doubt: A Parable' (Pulitzer-master label preserved per audit edit #3) vs 'Doubt' (Tony-master shorter label) even though both refer to the same play. Rewritten db_analog uses `INNER JOIN ON p.normalized_play_id = t.normalized_play_id` where normalized_play_id = `normalize_play_identity(play_title)` — a normalization function that collapses subtitle variants + minor label form differences to a canonical play key. This honestly models the cross-master label-form-tolerance that the staged Play column already encodes (per Pulitzer-master-labels-preserved policy). Update propagated to draft.json temporal_note + _extraction_notes.

normalization_decisions.rule: Play title verbatim from Wikipedia 'Pulitzer Prize for Drama' master labels per cycle-1 audit required edit #3. Subtitle preservation: 'Doubt: A Parable' (NOT shorter 'Doubt' Tony-master label); 'Angels in America: Millennium Approaches' (Part One specificity — disambiguates from 'Angels in America: Perestroika' Part Two which won Tony 1994 but not Pulitzer); 'August: Osage County' (colon-subtitle convention). 'J.B.' staged with initials+period convention per Pulitzer master (MacLeish's verse drama). 'Long Day's Journey into Night' apostrophe + lowercase 'into' verbatim per master.

Playwright verbatim from Wikipedia 'Pulitzer Prize for Drama' master with one cross-master normalization: co-authored plays use semicolon-delim per benchmark convention. The Diary of Anne Frank's 'Albert Hackett; Frances Goodrich' is the only co-authored row in the 19-row universe; Hackett-first ordering matches Pulitzer master's verbatim credit order. Single-author plays use master's exact name form including middle names where present ('Frank D. Gilroy' / 'John Patrick Shanley' / 'Branden Jacobs-Jenkins' hyphenated surname). Distinct same-surname playwrights preserved: 'Jason Miller' (That Championship Season 1973) ≠ 'Arthur Miller' (Death of a Salesman 1949) — both staged with full first name from Pulitzer master.

Integer year of Pulitzer Drama announcement per Wikipedia 'Pulitzer Prize for Drama' master. Pulitzer Drama announcements typically in April for the prior season's plays. Range: 1949 (Death of a Salesman) → 2025 (Purpose). Year-form is the announcement year (matches Pulitzer master's column convention).

Integer year of Tony ceremony per Wikipedia 'Tony Award for Best Play' master. Tony ceremony typically in June. 18 of 19 rows have Tony Year = Pulitzer Year (most dual-winner plays win both prizes within the same calendar year cycle). EDGE: Clybourne Park (Norris, row 18) has Pulitzer Year=2011 + Tony Year=2012 — the only 1-year-offset case in the staged 19-row universe. The offset reflects Clybourne Park's production trajectory (2010 Off-Broadway debut → 2011 Pulitzer announcement → 2012 Broadway transfer → 2012 Tony ceremony eligibility). Both years staged separately preserving the source-extractive cell values.

open_questions.question: Why use winner-row intersection instead of the Pulitzer master's '†' dagger marker?
open_questions.answer: Per cycle-1 audit required edit #2. The Pulitzer master's notes describe '†' as marking 'plays that also won Tony Best Play' — but the Pulitzer table includes BOTH winner rows AND finalist rows for each year, and the dagger appears on Tony-winning rows REGARDLESS of Pulitzer winner/finalist status. 2003 Pulitzer table example: winner row 'Anna in the Tropics' (Cruz) has no dagger; finalist rows 'The Goat or Who Is Sylvia?' (Albee, 2002 Tony) and 'Take Me Out' (Greenberg, 2003 Tony) BOTH carry '†' because they won Tony Best Play in their respective years even though they were Pulitzer finalists not winners. Dagger-only filtering would incorrectly include 2003 Pulitzer finalists alongside the Pulitzer winner — overcounts. Explicit winner-row intersection is the correct operational predicate.

open_questions.question: Why staged from Pulitzer master labels instead of Tony master labels?
open_questions.answer: Per cycle-1 audit required edit #3. Pulitzer master labels preserve subtitle specificity (Doubt: A Parable + Angels in America: Millennium Approaches Part-One disambiguation) while Tony master sometimes uses shorter common forms. Pulitzer Drama citation is the canonical scholarly reference for play identity; Tony Award page-link form may abbreviate. Staging Pulitzer-verbatim avoids Angels in America Part-One/Part-Two confusion (Part Two 'Perestroika' won 1994 Tony but NOT Pulitzer; NOT in 19-row universe).

open_questions.question: Why is Who's Afraid of Virginia Woolf? (Albee 1963) excluded?
open_questions.answer: Won Tony Best Play 1963 but the Pulitzer board declined to award any Drama Pulitzer that year overruling the jury's recommendation. Pulitzer winner-row membership is false; intersection-membership is false. Tests benchmark's strict-source-rendering policy.

open_questions.question: Why is Sunday in the Park with George (Sondheim/Lapine 1985) excluded? It won Pulitzer Drama.
open_questions.answer: Won Pulitzer Drama 1985 but it's a MUSICAL — won Tony Best Musical not Tony Best Play. Tony Awards have separate Best Play and Best Musical categories. Tony Best Play winner-row membership is false for any musical. {Pulitzer Drama} ∩ {Tony Best Play} auto-excludes all musical Pulitzer Drama winners without explicit musical filter. Other musical Pulitzer Drama winners also auto-excluded: Rent (Larson 1996), Next to Normal (Yorkey/Kitt 2010), Hamilton (Miranda 2016), A Strange Loop (Jackson 2020).

open_questions.question: Why does Clybourne Park have Pulitzer Year=2011 but Tony Year=2012?
open_questions.answer: Production trajectory: Off-Broadway debut 2010 → Pulitzer Drama announcement April 2011 (Off-Broadway eligibility) → Broadway transfer 2012 → Tony eligibility opened with Broadway transfer → Tony Best Play 2012 ceremony June 2012. The 1-year offset is master-source-canonical (both years are correct per their respective masters). This is the ONLY 1-year-offset case in the 19-row staged universe; all 18 other rows have Pulitzer Year = Tony Year. Tests benchmark's per-cell year-extraction precision.

open_questions.question: What's the database structure of the set_operation framing?
open_questions.answer: Per cycle-2-rewritten db_analog: pulitzer_drama_winners CTE = Pulitzer master rows with is_winner=TRUE (filters out finalist rows alongside the dagger-bearing rows) projected with `normalize_play_identity(play_title) AS normalized_play_id`; tony_best_play_winners CTE = Tony master rows with category='Best Play' AND is_winner=TRUE (filters out nominees) similarly normalized; INNER JOIN on normalized_play_id yields the 19-row dual-winner set; final SELECT extracts Play (Pulitzer-master label per audit edit #3), Playwright, Pulitzer Year, Tony Year ordered by Pulitzer Year ASC + Play ASC tiebreak. The INNER JOIN on normalized_play_id is semantically equivalent to INTERSECT on the canonical play-identity dimension; the cycle-1 original db_analog used raw play_title join which would have miss-matched 'Doubt: A Parable' (Pulitzer-master label) vs 'Doubt' (Tony-master shorter label) even though both refer to the same play — cycle-2 audit HYGIENE fix corrected this by introducing the normalized_play_id intermediate. The set-operation INTERSECT semantic is preserved with cross-master label-form-tolerance.
